PLAYBOOK -- design X-demo (carried under E-9004, registration REG-demo)
The declaration: prereg/X-demo_playbook.json, sha256 221664a07bcde4f8b91860b244e4d3f9c6f0ca8608eb470f817a5a7a40256753; its carrying record: prereg/X-demo_carried.json (pinned in E-9004); the joint held-out test's accepted result: results/heldout_x.csv (commit abc1234def).

HAND ENTRY ONLY. You enter every order yourself, by hand, on the firm's platform. Nothing in this playbook or its alerts places, sends or automates an order: no automated or API order entry, ever (it gets prop accounts banned).
NEVER HOLD OPPOSITE POSITIONS AT ONCE across your accounts or firms. While any position is open in any of your accounts, a new trade is taken only on that position's side; otherwise skip it.
One trade goes to one account. Never copy a trade to several accounts.
Never put size into major news: no entry and no working order inside a news window; a position open when a window starts is closed at its start.
No price is printed here: every order is stated against what you read on your platform when the alert reaches you. Bars are named by their stamp, the minute they open, as platforms label them.

FIRM AND PLAN
Firm: topstep; plan: 50K Trading Combine (as the firm's verified rules name it); instrument: MNQ.
Accounts, in the account order:
  - ts_a: an evaluation account (the Trading Combine); at most 50 contracts of MNQ open at once (the firm's verified limit).
  - ts_b: a funded account (the Express Funded Account; its scaling plan's entry tier, the lowest, bounds the size); at most 20 contracts of MNQ open at once (the firm's verified limit).
  - ts_c: an evaluation account (the Trading Combine); at most 50 contracts of MNQ open at once (the firm's verified limit).

COMPONENTS (one session window each; times in CT, Chicago)
Component asia_brk -- session asia: orders go live on the bars stamped 0 to 55 minutes after the session's start (its local open, 09:00 Asia/Tokyo, converted on each date):

  Trigger (rl3): pre-session tickets at the day's levels of one kind, fixed when the alert is sent, before the regular session's first fill; the tickets of a kind make one trade (the first to fill), unfilled tickets cancelled at the cutoff.

The no-harm floor's file: results/noharm_x.csv (commit abc1234def): the trigger's own side against the coin's on the real path, same fills, no redraw; the margin 0.05 is the one pinned under E-9000; each component's side passed: its composite not below the coin's by more than the margin.

EXECUTION RULES (every component)
- One position or working entry order at a time per firm (one level kind's tickets count as one order); after a position closes, wait at least 5 minutes before the next entry.
- Limit orders work 30 minutes from going live, then are cancelled.
- A limit or stop that would fill at once when it goes live (a BUY limit at or above the market, a SELL limit at or below it, a BUY stop at or below it, a SELL stop at or above it) is not placed: no trade.
- Closed window: no entry and no fill on the bars stamped 08:30 CT through 08:59 CT, every day.
- On a jobs-report day: no fill on the bars stamped up to 07:35 CT.
- No new entry after 15:08 CT. Flatten every position by the close of the bar stamped 15:07 CT (it ends at 15:08 CT) at the latest.
- A working order is cancelled when a news or closed window starts; an open position is closed at its start.
News windows (no entry and no fill inside them), from the synthetic release record:
  - CPI (synthetic record key): released at 07:30 CT; the window covers the bars stamped from 2 minutes before the release to 7 minutes after it; on 2021-03-16, 2021-04-07.
  - a synthetic afternoon release: released at 12:00 CT; the window covers the bars stamped from 3 minutes before the release to 6 minutes after it; on 2021-03-17.
Void days (no trade from the components named; all known before the alert):
  - an FOMC statement day: no trade at all that day.
  - an exchange holiday or a scheduled early close before the day's flatten: no trade that day.
  - the day after a scheduled early close, a scheduled closure (a weekday the exchange is shut) or a contract roll: no trade from a component that reads the previous day's levels.
  - 2021-03-19: an exchange holiday or a scheduled early close before the day's flatten: no trade that day.

ACCOUNT ROTATION
Rule by_component: each component's trades go to its own pool of accounts below, the one waiting longest first (a component without a pool uses every account). Each alert names the account the rule picks among the accounts you hold that day.
  component am_tix: ts_a, ts_c
  component pm_brk: ts_b
One trade goes to one account. Never copy a trade to several accounts.

THE BANKROLL STOP
Budget: $1700 (set under E-9000). When your total spending on this plan reaches it before a first payout, stop: buy no further evaluation and no reset, add no money, and keep trading only the accounts you already hold until each is passed or lost.

THE EXPECTED JOURNEY
From the result file results/journey_x.csv (commit abc1234def), measured on this declaration:
  - sessions to the first payout: 37.5 (search years: the years this design was chosen on, so likely better than what follows; median)
    its held-out reading is not named here: read it beside before trusting this figure.
  - chance of running out at the budget: 0.1234 (search years: the years this design was chosen on, so likely better than what follows; value)
    its held-out reading is not named here: read it beside before trusting this figure.
  - bankroll needed, unlucky tenth: 6250 (search years: the years this design was chosen on, so likely better than what follows; p90)
  - bankroll needed, unlucky tenth: 6611.5 (held-out years, reported beside, never judged; p90)
These figures were measured with every trade's direction replaced by a fair coin (zero edge), over many start days: they are what the account policy gives without any skill in direction. Your own journey will differ.
The backtests behind these figures also left out, for data reasons you cannot see and need not judge (research filters, not trading rules):
  - days whose stored bars end before the walk's last bar, end early or carry a data defect, and the day after one, or after a gap in the stored days.
  - overnight sessions with too many stored minutes missing.
